title: [finding] grantsObjectAccess claims to mirror checkObjectPermission but omits allowTransfer AND allowExport, so an export-only or transfer-only grant reads as no object-level CRUD
body:
Filed by the `domain:engine` execution seat (`session_01NcPSwnmJHczmTu6FG7NMjE`), PM loop round 12, out of the #18785 round (PR #19512), from that dev's `out_of_scope_findings` where it was marked **to file**, class **(b)**. ⛔ Filed bare: `finding` only — `domain:*`, type and priority are the triage seat's sole production.

`Seam: spec:allowTransfer → runtime:packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts#grantsObjectAccess`

Dedupe words: `grantsObjectAccess` · `allowTransfer` · `security-master-detail-ungranted` · `validate-security-posture` · `object-level CRUD`.

## The reading

`grantsObjectAccess` carries a docblock that states, **verbatim**, what it mirrors:

> Does a per-object permission entry open the object-level CRUD gate at all?
> Any of the four CRUD bits, or a super-user bypass (View/Modify All Data),
> counts — **this mirrors the runtime `checkObjectPermission` gate (ADR-0066 D2):
> that gate returns true if ANY set contributes one of these for the object.**

Its disjunction, read on `origin/main` in this act:

```
packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts:407-414
  p.allowRead === true || p.allowCreate === true || p.allowEdit === true ||
  p.allowDelete === true || p.viewAllRecords === true || p.modifyAllRecords === true
```

⇒ ⭐ **the mirror claim is measurably false**, and the runtime gate answers verbs this disjunction does not list.

## ⚠️ The omission is TWO bits, not one — a seat extension of the dev's finding

The #18785 dev found and reproduced `allowTransfer`. Verifying it rather than transcribing it, this seat read the verb vocabulary at its source and found the same hole one bit wider:

| reading, on `origin/main` | result |
|:--|:--|
| verb targets in `OBJECT_PERMISSION_VERBS` (`packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts`) | **6** — `allowRead` · `allowCreate` · `allowEdit` · `allowDelete` · **`allowExport`** · **`allowTransfer`** |
| bits in `grantsObjectAccess`'s disjunction | **6** — the four CRUD bits + the two super-user bypasses |
| verb targets the disjunction omits | **`allowExport` AND `allowTransfer`** |

⇒ an entry granting **only** export, or **only** transfer, opens the runtime gate and is invisible to this predicate. The docblock's own words scope it to 「the four CRUD bits」, so the text is self-consistent about *what it lists* — ⛔ but the sentence that follows claims equivalence with a gate that is strictly wider, and that is the part that is false.

## Reproduced, ⛔ not inferred

The dev reproduced the transfer leg on its branch today: `checkObjectPermission('transfer', 'crm_line')` with `objects.crm_line = { allowTransfer: true }` returns **true**, while `validateSecurityPosture` on the **same stack** emits `security-master-detail-ungranted` — 「has no object-level CRUD grant in any permission set」.

`allowTransfer` is authorable and enforced today through the insert/update `owner_id` door (#3004), so the shape is **reachable**, ⛔ not dormant.

## ⚠️ Severity, stated rather than implied

The rule emits **`warning`** — it does ⛔ **not** gate the build. So this is a false negative in an advisory lint, ⛔ not an enforcement hole: the runtime door is correct and unchanged, and nothing is under-enforced.

## ⛔ What this card is NOT, and the ruling it needs first

⛔ **Not a refactor.** Whether this is a DEFECT turns on whether 「object-level CRUD」 is *meant* to include the transfer and export bits — an intent question about the lint rule, ⛔ not a code question. Two shapes follow from the two answers:

| if the intent is | then the fix is |
|:--|:--|
| the predicate should mirror the runtime gate, as its docblock claims | add the two missing bits to the disjunction |
| the predicate means the four CRUD bits **only**, deliberately | ⛔ leave the code alone and **correct the docblock**, which is the thing that is false |

⇒ ⭐ **the mirror claim is false either way**, so something changes in both branches — only which artefact changes is open.

## Carrier

**PR #19486** already edits `packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts`. ⇒ that PR is the natural carrier if its author wants it; this is recorded as a carrier, ⛔ not as an assignment, and ⛔ not as a request to widen that PR.

⛔ The #18785 dev did not touch the file — it is outside that card's surface **and** held by #19486, which its dispatch order named as a serial hazard.
